justification: Gap (1) completes a fixed collocation, “to take the long ___,” after “which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key” — i.e. accept a long-term perspective. Only “view” forms that idiom; “take the long outlook/gaze/sight” are not English collocations, and “gaze” and “sight” are literal looking. C.

Gap (2) heads a rule-as-written statement that the next sentences set against practice: “That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd. It is simply not what the list runs on.” “Strictly” (strictly speaking, by the rule) is exactly that move. “Curiously” is blocked by “nobody... finds it odd”; “Increasingly” asserts a trend the passage never gives; “Privately” contradicts a written clause. B.

Gap (3) is inside a named idiom — “The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men’s ___” — and the only phrase in English is “dead men’s shoes,” waiting for a place that falls vacant on a death. It matches the surrounding sense: “Movement comes when somebody else stops... a winter that settles it,” and “It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke.” Coats, gloves and hats form no such phrase. A.

Gap (4) sits in a two-pole concession: “the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either,” so the gap needs the opposite pole of approving. “Censorious” supplies it; “gracious” sits on the approving side and makes the contrast collapse, while “cautious” and “anxious” are not opposites of approval at all. The context — a tenancy quietly passing to a nephew, given “one line” in the minutes — is the committee neither blessing nor condemning. D.

Gap (5) takes a rule as object: “The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___.” Rules are invoked; the point is that after “Three times the answer was no” the rule was never applied. “Summoned” takes people, “provoked” takes reactions, and “evoked” takes memories or feelings — the near-homophone trap. C.

The passage says height, not pattern, carries information: “The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack.” That is A. B is contradicted by the stated reason for a narrow mouth — “since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening” (rain and birds are never mentioned); C by “Pattern tells you very little”; D by “Builders’ yards sold whatever was in stock” and “a stack rebuilt in 1961 carries what came off the lorry.”

The figures are the whole item: the chandler’s hatch “opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller’s opened at two and took in 390,” and “Both shut when the evening cart went at eight” — thirteen hours against six for twenty-two more letters. That kills B (412 vs 390 is not “far more”) and C (both shut at eight, so the bookseller stayed open after nothing). A is the strongest near-miss, since the keeper “was allowed threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves,” but it says “the keepers” stretched their hours and the bookseller “opened at two” — a six-hour day — so it is not supported for both. D is what the near-equal counts against unequal hours imply.

The writer withdraws her vote but not the need: “Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst” against “Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”, closing with “Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten” — equipment yes, fee-funding no. B is contradicted by the cut line, the short ladder and the absent defibrillator; C by the retraction; A by the fact that her objection is to the mechanism, not the level (“Avgiften vid bryggan lär förskjuta en del av badandet just dit”). D.

The one figure given is “Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna” — so roughly sixty-nine per cent, about seven nights in ten, went unpaid. C inverts it; B is contradicted by the fact that the follow-up produced a number at all; D is never mentioned — the sign is described as still the model (“en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar”). A.

What the anmälningar showed is stated plainly: “I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv.” A is the opposite of that; C is contradicted by “Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord”; B goes past the evidence, since the text says the strikeouts “kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning – materialet svarar inte på det”. D.

She concedes: “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar” — and that nearest explanation was the ordinary one, “Den förklaring som ligger närmast är fåfänga.” A is contradicted by “Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt”; D by “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns”, which leaves nothing to combine; C overreads the residue — “Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop” concerns loose details, not the main question, which she does settle. B.

The writer withdraws her vote while conceding the need: "Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst", "Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga", and her closing prescription "Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten" — equipment yes, fee no, i.e. D. B is refuted by the same "ingen stridsfråga" sentence plus the cut boj line and the stege that "slutar en halvmeter ovanför vattenytan". C is what she voted for and now retracts. A is the trap for a careless reader: she attacks the calculation ("Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent") to show fees will not collect, never to argue for a larger sum.

The only figure given for the ställplats is "Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna" — 69 per cent unpaid, which A renders as roughly seven nights in ten. C states the arithmetic opposite. B is contradicted by the fact that the municipality did measure it and reported a number. D imports an outcome the text never mentions: the sign, code and open grind are described as still standing ("en grind som står öppen hela säsongen"), and the writer's point is that the same design would work even worse at the bryggan.

The archive finding is stated plainly: "I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv" — D, hedge and all. A is the kassör hypothesis she abandons ("Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså"). C is refuted by "Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd". B is the strongest wrong answer because the twenty-odd strikeovers are real, but the text refuses precisely that reading: "överstrykningarna kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning — materialet svarar inte på det".

She concedes: "Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar" — the nearest explanation being "fåfänga", so she drops her own suspicion for the ordinary account: B. A is contradicted by "Där hade jag fel" and by the concession itself. D invents a both-and settlement the text never offers; she reports that none of her three mechanisms existed. C is the tempting near-miss, since "Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop" — but those are named residuals (the hemmansägare, the widows, the strikeovers), not a refusal to decide the main question, which she does decide.

The gap completes the fixed idiom "take the long view", the tone set by the sentence before it: "which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key", and by "in the politest possible terms" — C. A is the near-synonym trap: "outlook" shares the sense of prospect but does not take "take the long ___"; one has a long-term outlook, one does not take one. B and D fail on both idiom and sense — "gaze" and "sight" are literal acts of looking, and neither carries the patience-with-a-slow-process meaning the paragraph needs.

The paragraph sets the written rule against the lived practice: "___, a plot cannot be inherited. The tenancy ends when the tenant does ... That is the clause as written ... It is simply not what the list runs on", which is the classic "Strictly, ..." concessive frame: B. C is pre-empted by the very next clause, "nobody disputes it or finds it odd" — the text denies the oddity that "Curiously" would assert. A needs a trend the passage never reports (the clause is stable, not increasingly true), and D would mean unofficially or in confidence, the opposite of a clause as written.

The sentence signposts a known phrase — "The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men's ___" — and the idiom is "dead men's shoes", matching the context of movement only when somebody stops ("a knee that will not manage the walk from the gate"). B, C and D are all wearable items chosen to look parallel, but none is an English idiom, and the follow-up "It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke" only makes sense of a phrase readers already recognise. "Gloves" is the most seductive of the three given all the digging, yet it names no waiting-for-a-vacancy expression at all.

The frame is a two-sided denial: "the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either", so the gap must hold the opposite pole of approval — disapproval, i.e. "censorious": D. A collapses the structure: "gracious" is on the approving side, so "not approving, but not gracious either" denies the same pole twice and says nothing. B and C name attitudes on an unrelated axis (care, worry); neither contrasts with approval, and neither fits minutes that "give it one line" about a tenancy transfer the committee tolerates without endorsing.

The rule exists on paper but has never been applied: "The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___" — "invoked" is the collocation for a rule being called upon: C. D is the sound-alike trap: "evoked" means to call up a feeling or memory and takes no rule as object. A would need a person or a meeting, not a clause, and B ("provoked") reverses the direction — a rule provokes a reaction, it is not itself provoked; the point is that three refusals passed without consequence.

The one diagnostic the writer endorses is height: "Height is the part worth reading. The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack" — a badly drawing flue, which is A. C inverts the passage's opening judgement, "Pattern tells you very little", and D is refuted by the same lines — yards "sold whatever was in stock" and ornament served "to tell their own door from thirty identical ones". B is the plausible real-world fact the text specifically does not give: the narrowing is explained aerodynamically, "since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening", with no mention of rain or birds.

The numbers only reconcile one way: the chandler's hatch "opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390", and "Both shut when the evening cart went at eight" — thirteen hours against six for a 22-letter difference, so volume tracks the cart's hour, not the hours open: D. B calls 412 versus 390 "far more", which the figures contradict. C is impossible because both shut at eight with the cart. A is the strongest wrong reading, since the keeper drew "threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves" — but the bookseller opened only at two, so no such stretching by both keepers is shown, and no motive is stated anywhere in the returns or the surveyor's note.

A is unsupported (no price series is tracked across the nine harvests) and C is absent entirely. B names only Grendisham's single objection ("nobody was there to see it early"), a strand of the dispute rather than its subject.

The swab result is stated once and plainly: "His team swabbed the duct faces of twenty-six machines that had never burned; per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent." That contradicts A directly, and C is never addressed (no claim about newest ducts). D misreads the dispute: Grendisham disputes the swabs on seasonality — "her crews still pull buckets of fines in February from machines that swabbed clean in September" — not on sample size, and the writer treats them as the strong evidence ("The swabs are hard to walk past").

Grendisham's objection is that the log's second timestamp is a discovery time, not an ignition time: "The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught." A is the opposite of her point — she says pairing the two numbers is why "of course the fire looks late". B and D are not addressed: she never restricts the log to her own service customers and never says the times were not meant as evidence.

Steadgrove's date sort is the implication: "Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, he argues, and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing" — a pressure of the calendar, not of the equipment. B overstates the count (49 of 61 leaves twelve fires outside the stretch, which is not "hardly a fire"); C is contradicted by "Steadgrove's is not the mutual's to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators"; D is never claimed — "trucks waiting" appears only in the closing question about one operator, and no arrival-versus-capacity comparison is made.

The writer's verdict is explicit: "Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these" and "Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it." That kills A (the objections stand) and B (she does adjudicate — "The swabs are hard to walk past"). D is contradicted by the reservation about his remedy: "Whether writing a run-on clause into next year's policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check."

Sekvensen står i första stycket: "Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över ... Först därefter rostades den på en bädd av ved." A vänder både årstiden och ordningen (rostning före hög). B motsägs av "Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt", och D av "Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte."

Tolvsäter's first clear result states both the effect and its mechanism: "De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan i stället för att låta sig sträckas." B inverts the direction of the relationship. C overstates it — the harder runs gave brittler blooms, not failure of "samtliga blåsningar". D belongs to the excavation description ("Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt"), not to the trials, whose reported findings are the two above.

The solid-state reduction is named as the governing fact and is then explicitly made to govern both consequences: "Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt. Järnet reducerades i fast form ... Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn" and "Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen." A is contradicted by the dating "tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet"; B inverts the technologies, since it is the later hyttan that "krävde vattenkraft"; C is contradicted by "uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen."

The trials reinterpret the iron-rich slag as a precondition rather than a loss: "Och den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla ... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet." A is Krokvall's reading of "dålig kontroll", which is precisely what "det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot" rejects. C is contradicted by "Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt", and D by "varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen" — the text leaves the yield variation unexplained.

The article opens on the settled county view — “the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns” and “The explanation is as settled as the count” — and then spends four paragraphs on a fight over the why: Calverend “thinks the count is right and the reason is wrong”, Grendisham defends the fines, Steadgrove moves the cause “one step further out, to the contract”. That is exactly a familiar rule about which dryers burn plus a disputed account of why (D). A is impossible: the only price mentioned is “so much per ton per point of moisture”, one clause of background, and no movement across nine harvests is ever described. C is not in the text at all — nobody argues that small farms should dry their own crop; custom operations appear as an explanation of the count, not as a recommendation to avoid them. B is the strongest wrong answer and still fails: the difficulty of investigating unmanned sites is Grendisham’s single objection inside one paragraph (“It looks late because nobody was there to see it early”), a move in the argument rather than the argument, and it would leave the swabs, the cleaning advice and Steadgrove’s whole contract case unexplained.

Stated outright: “per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent” — equally dusty inside (B). A is the exact reverse of that sentence and is the belief the swabs destroyed: “The county’s standard advice rests on a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show.” C fails twice: no option-relevant claim about “newest” ducts exists anywhere in the passage, and “Nothing at all” contradicts a measurable per-square-foot load being reported for both types. D is the most tempting distractor — twenty-six does sound small — but no one in the piece attacks the sample size; the writer calls the swabs the settled part (“The swabs are hard to walk past”), Steadgrove “accepts the swabs”, and Grendisham’s counter is about persistence over a season (“machines that swabbed clean in September”), not about how many machines were sampled.

Grendisham’s point is precisely a noticed-versus-started distinction: “The other time in the file is the moment the call came in. On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught” (C). A is the opposite of “Set those two numbers side by side and of course the fire looks late” — the divergence between the controller log and the call time is her entire objection, not an agreement. B is invented: her crews’ coverage is mentioned only for the fines buckets, never as a limit on the fire department’s log, and the log is the county’s, not hers. D overreaches in a different direction: she does not say the log was never meant as evidence — she reads it as evidence and argues it is being read wrongly, which is why she calls the clock “the weak joint in the argument” rather than the log worthless.

The nine days are defined by conditions that attach to the calendar, not to hardware: “when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator’s delivery window is closing”, which is why Steadgrove can say “Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine … and the machine stops mattering.” That is the implication in A — in that stretch the commercial squeeze is common to everyone drying, whatever machine they own, and it is the working-through, not the dryer, that fills the log. B is a quantifier overreach: “Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch” out of sixty-one leaves twelve fires outside it, roughly one in five, which no reader may compress into “Hardly a fire”. C is flatly contradicted — “Steadgrove’s is not the mutual’s to give, since the deduction schedule belongs to the elevators”. D is never asserted: the closing scene has “trucks waiting” for one operator on one night, which is not a claim that intake outruns drying capacity across those days.

The writer adjudicates explicitly in the last paragraph and lands on untested-but-consistent: “Until then Calverend’s account fits the evidence without having been tested by it” (C). A is contradicted one sentence earlier — “Grendisham’s objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these”. B is the trap for a reader who mistakes even-handedness for abstention, but she does rule: she settles the swabs (“nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground”), separates out the clock (“The clock is another matter”), and states the standing of Calverend’s account. D inverts the closing move: the run-on clause is raised as an open question the mutual must settle — “Whether writing a run-on clause into next year’s policies would be worth anything turns on something nobody has worked out how to check” — not as something she is convinced of.

Ordningen står ordagrant i första stycket: “Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan”, malmen “fick ligga ute vintern över, tills frosten hade sprängt sönder klumparna”, och “Först därefter rostades den på en bädd av ved” — alltså C. A är fel på båda punkterna samtidigt: fel årstid (senhöst, inte vårvinter) och omkastad ordning, eftersom rostningen uttryckligen kommer efter vinterns liggtid, inte före högläggningen. B motsägs direkt av “Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt”. D motsägs av “Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte”, och blot mark är dessutom själva villkoret man väntade bort — arbetet gjordes när vattnet sjunkit undan.

Försökens första resultat: “De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan i stället för att låta sig sträckas” — hårdare drift, sprödare järn, och orsaken är just att kol gick in i metallen (A). B kastar om sambandet och har inget stöd alls; ingenstans sägs att svagare drift gav sprödhet. C är en absolut överdrift: texten säger att luppen sprack under släggan vid hård drift, inte att “Samtliga” av trettiosex blåsningar misslyckades — tvärtom redovisas två tydliga resultat, inte ett haveri. D förväxlar textavsnitt: torkningen och murningen (“Innan den kunde fyllas måste den torkas långsamt”) hör till beskrivningen av ugnstypen, inte till vad Tolvsäters blåsningar visade, där “Två resultat är tydliga” räknar upp sprödheten och slaggens järnhalt.

Texten gör fastformsreduktionen till förklaringsgrund: “Järnet reducerades i fast form … en seg, porös lupp”, därefter “Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn” och “Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt, i räckningen” — exakt både luppens storlek och arbetets tyngdpunkt (D). A sträcker kronologin förbi det texten tillåter: “Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet”, och 1880-talet förekommer bara som uppteckningar om mossar och ägande, inte som pågående blästbruk. B är omvänt: det är hyttan, “som kom senare”, som “krävde vattenkraft och ständig drift”, medan blästugnen “kostade lera, sten och ved”. C motsägs ordagrant av “uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen”.

Slutsatsen dras åt villkorshållet: “Och den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla … Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet” (B). A är Krokvalls tolkning — “ett tecken på dålig kontroll” — och den är just den som underkänns: “det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot”. C motsägs ordagrant av “Krokvalls mätvärden har ingen ifrågasatt”, och Tolvsäter presenteras aldrig som en konkurrerande mätserie utan som praktiska försök. D är den lockande halvsanningen: varphögarna är mycket riktigt stora, men texten lämnar uttryckligen spridningen i utbyte oförklarad — “varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen” — så att härleda skillnaderna mellan platser ur järnförlusten är att gå förbi texten.

findings.quote: A familiar rule about which dryers burn, and a disputed account of why.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY; blind pick D. The unit's sibling stems name duct swabs on mixed-flow dryers, a fire department log, the nine days at the end of harvest and 'Calverend's explanation', which together identify the subject as dryer fires plus a contested cause - option D almost verbatim. Not lethal: cross-stem topic corroboration fires on authentic main-idea items too, so it is a flag rather than a structural leak.

findings.quote: The case for small farms drying their crop rather than paying to have it done.
findings.note: C is the only advocacy-framed option in a set whose other stems are all attribution, measurement and logs, and A names a price series no other stem touches; a reader with no domain knowledge drops both on register and topic alone, leaving two.

findings.quote: Nothing at all had gathered on the newest ducts.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY; blind pick A. 'Nothing at all' is an unstripped extreme absolute and the only categorical claim among the four, so a no-expertise solver drops C on the absolutizer heuristic before reading anything.

findings.quote: The two kinds of dryers came out about equally dusty inside.
findings.note: A and B are exact contradictories on the one comparison the unit turns on, and q1's option D already advertises 'a familiar rule about which dryers burn'; a null result would leave the named investigator nothing to explain, so the pair resolves toward A without the passage. Narrative inference, not a form-only mechanism - flag, not kill.

findings.quote: They mark when a fire was noticed, not when it began.
findings.note: Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick C. Ordinary knowledge that fire-brigade logs timestamp detection or call-out rather than ignition decides this with no passage; the distractors are substantive positions, so this is normal test design routed to adjudication.

findings.quote: They were never intended to be read as evidence at all.
findings.note: 'never ... at all' makes D the extreme twin of C's point - a residual absolute that a form-only solver strips, narrowing the field to three before any reading.

findings.quote: They line up closely with what the burner controllers show.
findings.note: A is a corroboration claim: if the log times simply agreed with the controllers there would be no reason for the text to quote a named source about them. Discourse-level elimination, available without the passage.

findings.quote: The mutual could slow the rush by rewriting the deduction schedule.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY; blind pick A. The stem asks what is implied about the nine days, but C's subject is what the mutual could do about them - a scope mismatch a reader with no domain knowledge can act on. C also reads as text content borrowed from the remedy that q5 alludes to, i.e. true-but-unresponsive.

findings.quote: Hardly a fire in the log fell outside that stretch.
findings.note: The stem asks what is 'implied'; B is a datum the text would state outright, so it is off-shape. That leaves A and D, and the question is not decided between them without the passage.

findings.quote: Growers face the same commercial pressure then, whatever they own.
findings.note: Round-2 de-absolutization checked: A still carries a universalising frame ('the same ... whatever they own') while B is now hedged ('Hardly a fire'), so the absolutizer heuristic points away from A while the 'implied' shape heuristic points toward it. The two tells cross rather than align, which is what keeps the question alive; no option pair here stands in an entailment relation, though A and D can both be true at once, thinning the discriminator between them.

findings.quote: She thinks it fits the facts but has not been tested.
findings.note: Blind class PARTIALLY; blind pick C. C is the only two-sided option against three committed stances, so the standard 'the qualified option wins an author-attitude item' heuristic points at it with zero domain knowledge. This is the unit's most form-driven surface and worth adjudication attention.

findings.quote: She stays out of it and leaves the reader to decide.
findings.note: B is what stops this being a clean structural leak: strict authorial neutrality is an equally canonical attitude key, so form narrows the field to B vs C but does not decide it. Kill bar not met.

findings.quote: She is convinced enough to want his remedy written into next year’s policies.
findings.note: Round-2 repair verified: D now sits on an action/advocacy axis and no longer entails C - wanting a remedy legislated does not assert that it 'has not been tested', and C's untested clause is not implied by any other option. Every pair in this question was checked; no entailment survives. A and D remain strippable as over-commitments, which is the source of the two eliminations above.

findings.quote: Malmen togs upp på vårvintern, medan tjälen bar, och rostades innan den lades i hög.
findings.note: Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick A. Standard knowledge of Swedish bog-ore working - the bog is worked while the frost bears and the ore is roasted before it is stockpiled - picks A over C without the passage. C is a substantive rival practice (winter weathering), so this is world-knowledge answerability, not a leak.

findings.quote: Varje mosse i socknen bar ett skikt som kunde tas upp med samma redskap.
findings.note: Residual universal quantifier ('Varje ... samma redskap'): a solver with no expertise strips B on the absolutizer heuristic alone.

findings.quote: Ibland kunde malmen tas upp utan att skiktet först hade letats upp med spett, om marken var tillräckligt blöt.
findings.note: The stem asks about two steps - extraction and preparation - and only A and C answer both; B and D describe extraction alone. A shape mismatch that halves the field before any reading, then domain knowledge decides the remaining pair.

findings.quote: Att driva ugnarna hårdare gav ett sprödare järn, eftersom kolhalten i metallen steg.
findings.note: Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick A. A and B are exact physical inverses and textbook metallurgy settles them - a harder blast raises carbon pickup and carbon embrittles the iron - so school chemistry answers this with no passage. This is the most exploitable blind surface in the LAS unit; distractors remain substantive, so flag rather than kill.

findings.quote: Samtliga blåsningar misslyckades så snart bälgtagen blev tätare än vanligt.
findings.note: 'Samtliga' plus categorical failure is a residual absolute; C strips on form with no expertise.

findings.quote: Försöken gav framför allt besked om hur en ugn av den utgrävda typen bör muras och torkas.
findings.note: D is the meta-option - what the trials taught about method rather than what they showed - the conventional filler shape under a 'what emerged' stem, so it is the third elimination.

findings.quote: Att järnet vanns i fast form bestämde både luppens storlek och var tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg.
findings.note: Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick D. Knowing that the direct process reduces iron in the solid state - hence small blooms and labour concentrated in consolidating them - makes D true on its own terms; it is also the only 'both X and Y' option, the usual shape of a 'which statement agrees best' key.

findings.quote: Den äldre framställningen krävde vattenkraft, till skillnad från den som kom efter.
findings.note: B inverts a well-known chronology - water power belongs to the later blast-furnace works, not the older direct process - so any history-of-technology knowledge strips it blind.

findings.quote: Uppteckningarna från 1880-talet ger en fyllig bild av hur järnet en gång framställdes.
findings.note: Cross-stem corroboration: q2 establishes that reconstruction blasningar were needed at all, which argues the records are thin rather than 'fyllig'. C therefore falls without the passage.

findings.quote: Den var snarast ett villkor för att processen skulle fungera, eftersom en järnfattigare slagg blir trögflytande.
findings.note: Blind class WORLD_KNOWLEDGE; blind pick B. Bloomery slag is fayalitic and must stay iron-rich to run fluid at furnace temperature, so the option is correct as written and states its own mechanism; a reader with archaeometallurgy picks it blind. Distractors are substantive - flag, not kill.

findings.quote: Den visar att en betydande del av råvaran gick till spillo genom vårdslös hantering.
findings.note: 'vårdslös hantering' imputes negligence to the historical smelters; a blame-framed option is the standard distractor shape in this genre and strips on register alone, with no expertise.

findings.quote: Den är omtvistad, eftersom Tolvsäters mätningar har gett andra värden än Krokvalls.
findings.note: Round-2 repair verified: C is no longer doubly strippable - no absolute and no piled-up shape mismatch. One weakness remains: it is the only 'no conclusion is available' option under a stem that asks for a conclusion, and it introduces a Krokvall/Tolvsater dispute no other stem in the unit hints at, so it is still the easiest of the four to drop.

findings.quote: Den förklarar varför avfallshögarna blev så stora och, genom järnförlusten, varför utbytet skilde sig åt mellan platserna.
findings.note: Round-2 rebuild checked: D's inference is no longer invalid but is still loose - the iron content of the slag does not by itself explain heap size, which tracks slag volume, and 'mellan platserna' presumes between-site variation the singular 'jarnhalten' does not establish. All six option pairs were tested for entailment and none holds; B and D can nonetheless both be true at once, so their discriminator is framing rather than fact - a G-KEY/G-DISTRACTOR concern, not a blind-solvability leak.
